Package PCBN
============



# How to install

The release version on CRAN:

```r
install.packages("PCBN")
```

The development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("AlexisDerumigny/PCBN")
```


# Graph backends

PCBN supports `bnlearn` and `caugi` graphs. Existing calls continue to use
`bnlearn`. Install the optional `caugi` package to use its backend:

```r
install.packages("caugi")
```

Pass `graph_backend` to a function that accepts a DAG to select its backend.
PCBN converts the input graph before computation, so the same graph can be
used to compare both backends:

```{r}
library(PCBN)
DAG = bnlearn::model2network("[U1][U2|U1][U3|U2]")
dsep_set(DAG, "U1", "U3", "U2", graph_backend = "bnlearn")
if (requireNamespace("caugi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dsep_set(DAG, "U1", "U3", "U2", graph_backend = "caugi")
}
```

You can also build a native caugi graph:

```{r}
if (requireNamespace("caugi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  DAG = create_empty_DAG(3, graph_backend = "caugi")
  DAG = caugi::add_edges(DAG, from = "U1", edge = "-->", to = "U3")
  dsep_set(DAG, "U1", "U2")
}
```

When `graph_backend` is omitted, functions infer it from the input graph.
`new_PCBN()`, `fit_copulas()`, and `fit_all_orders()` accept the same argument.
PCBN objects store the selected native graph in `$DAG` and the backend name
in `$graph_backend`. Simulation, likelihood calculation, printing, and plotting
use that backend automatically. Graph repair also returns the selected native
graph type.

Conversions preserve node order and isolated nodes. Different backends may
use different valid topological orderings, so identical random seeds need not
produce identical simulated samples across backends. The caugi backend requires
version 1.3.0 or later; installing it from source requires a Rust toolchain.
